title: Four-beat rhythm, shuffle rhythm and tempos
summary: Early bands played four beats; the first shuffle rhythm he recalls was Henry Busse; tempos could be fast like Tiger Rag.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: What style would he play? Would he play just a straight four?

Yeah. Yeah. No, no, no. Those early bands, I don't remember them playing shuffle rhythm. The only one, the first band I remember playing shuffle rhythm was this trumpet player. Oh man. What is his name? Any of you gentlemen remember? Here in town? No, no, it was a nationally known orchestra. Henry Bussey? Henry Bussey. That's the first shuffle rhythm I can recall. Henry Bussey seemed to be the one to produce that. And these guys down here would play four or two of them? Oh, they'd just play a beat, man. Four beats. I mean, on a banjo or a string instrument in the rhythm section. They seemed to play that four beats.
When would they play two beats? If ever?

Well, I don't recall that. I don't recall. I'm trying to associate that beat with some of the tunes that I think about and I just can't. I can remember them just a nice flowing easy beat, four beats, you know. How fast? Well, naturally, it'd depend on the tempo. They'd change. You know, I mean, we'd play some tunes slow, some tunes would be medium, and then we'd play some pretty fast ones at times.
Did they play as fast then as they do today?

I think some of the tunes they did, like we associate a speedy tempo with Tiger Rag. Well, they played pretty well up in those days, too. I get a kick out of Lewis, some of those tempos he plays Tiger Rag. I think I have three or four records, the Masters, you know, that he made, and they all really going. Now, those...
